subject: Digimed private endpoint egress: classification, permitlist, and contract asks
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@digimed.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@digimed.com
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Digimed private endpoint egress - initial questions

Tessa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We're starting the internal checklist for the private deployment (VPC/private-runtime) integration and have a few concrete asks so we can move the network and procurement workstreams in parallel: 

1) Permitlist / IPs: please confirm whether Redwood can provide a stable set of public egress IPs we can allow in our perimeter firewall, or if you expect ephemeral NAT with a short rotation window. If static IPs are available, we need ASN/owner proof and the desired CIDR length.

2) Ports & protocols: can you confirm minimal outbound ports required for both control-plane and runtime (e.g., 443 + DNS/853)? Do you support SNI-based routing only or require full FQDN egress?

3) TLS / mTLS: our security team prefers mutual TLS for control-plane callbacks and webhook validation. Do you support mTLS from runtime -> control-plane and vice versa?

4) Fallback modes: if a customer restricts outbound IPs to an allowlist, what fallback routing do you provide for capacity spikes (canary to hosted, burst to shared)?

5) Evidence pack: procurement/security want a short proof pack we can attach to the SOW: sample permitlist format, evidence of IP ownership / ASN, and a short runbook for rotating IPs.

Attached: digimed_network_diagram.pdf (internal topology).

If we can get the first-pass answers today we'll schedule a quick call with our firewall team tomorrow morning.

Regards,
Raj Patel
NetOps Lead, Digimed Health
raj.patel@digimed.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@digimed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Digimed private endpoint egress - initial questions

Hi Raj —

Thanks, and great notes. Below is a concise, implementable checklist and the evidence we can provide. I've attached a CSV template you can drop into your ticketing system (redwood_private_egress_template.csv).

Operational summary (short):
- Control plane (management): outbound to redwood-control.redwood.com (443) — we support mTLS for the control channel.
- Runtime (model inference): outbound egress to model-fetch and telemetry endpoints — we recommend permitlisting the static SNAT IP pool we can assign per-tenant.

Permitlist & IP ownership
- We can offer a dedicated SNAT pool per customer in the US region: 2 static IPv4s (primary/secondary) by default; optional expansion to 4 on request.
- Ownership evidence: we will supply an IP manifest (ASN, WHOIS extract, and certificate where applicable) in the evidence bundle.

Ports / DNS / SNI
- Required outbound: TCP 443 (HTTPS), UDP/TCP 53 (DNS) or DNS-over-TLS 853 if you constrain DNS.
- SNI/FQDN: runtime uses SNI; permitlisting by SNI alone is not sufficient if your firewall drops TLS-inspecting traffic — static IPs required for strict allowlist setups.

mTLS & Identity
- Control-plane connections: mTLS supported. We will provide CA cert thumbprints and sample client certs for your Ops to validate.
- Runtime telemetry: TLS with server cert validation; client cert for telemetry available on request.

Fallback / capacity modes
- Primary: dedicated SNAT pool (recommended).
- Fallback 1: regional shared SNAT pool (read-only allowed for low-sensitivity workloads).
- Fallback 2: hosted routing via Redwood public endpoints (strictly last-resort; only for customers that opt into hosted fallback in contract).

Evidence pack & runbook
- We'll attach: IP manifest, permitlist CSV template (attached), short rotation runbook, and an exportable firewall snippet (.txt) you can paste into your rule set.

Next steps
1) I can join your firewall team call tomorrow 09:00 PT to walk through the snippet.
2) Please send your procurement contact (I see procurement@digimed.com in cc) and I'll drop the SOW redlines and DocuSign link for the dedicated-IP addendum.

Attached: redwood_private_egress_template.csv (CSV), high-level runbook stub (in the bundle).

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Tessa.Morgan@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0199

- We can allocate a default 2-IP SNAT pool for Digimed (US-West region). Expansion to 4 IPs is a one-time configuration and will be included as an addendum.
- Rotation window: we recommend 24h planned rotations; rotations due to infra work will be communicated as non-disruptive maintenance in the customer portal and are covered under standard enterprise SLAs unless otherwise negotiated.
- DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/AB12345CD67890 (dedicated-ip addendum).

Raj — ops/engineering side deck:

- We'll include an "egress fallback" runbook as part of the onboarding checklist. That runbook contains: health checks for permitlist hits, automated switch to regional shared SNAT pool, and a canary test to validate latency/RPS on fallback.
- For strict-permitlist customers we recommend implementing a short-lived canary route (5% of traffic) to a staged shared pool before full failover. This reduces risk if the customer blocks the shared pool.
- I'll attach the runbook stub (egress-fallback-runbook.md) and the firewall paste snippet separately; Tessa will present both on the call.
